# Engineering Criteria

The one owner of the bar code is judged and built against, and of how much effort building and checking it is worth. Callers load this file and the files its Packs table selects for what their work touches: `full-review` judges a codebase against them and owns how gaps become findings; `orchestrated-dev` slices and `root-cause` fixes meet them for what they change; scaffolding workflows hold generated code to them. A change meets the criteria for the code it adds or changes; gaps it discovers elsewhere follow the caller's discovered-work rule: the calling skill's own handling where it has one, else the global rules' Discovered work bullet (Minimal-Code Discipline) where installed, else the consuming repository's own rule; with none, report them to the user (an unattended run, through its caller) instead of fixing them. Security handling (held findings, disclosure) belongs to the calling skill or the global rules, and items in these files marked as security defects follow it; otherwise a discovered security or data-exposure defect goes only to the user, never into a tracked file, commit, PR, issue or comment text until the user decides how it is fixed, whatever a repository's general discovered-work rule says.

## Principles

- Value = likelihood x impact / effort. Act on what realistically breaks, leaks, costs or slows; keep designs pragmatic: no over-engineering, gold-plating, accommodations for unlikely cases, heavy validation of unlikely edge cases or defenses against states the types, callers or framework already rule out. Input crossing a trust boundary is never speculative or an unlikely edge case. Resilient designs win over clever ones: clever workarounds are built only when explicitly requested or required by these criteria, apart from an unavoidable, scoped and commented third-party mitigation; security, accessibility, data-loss and trust-boundary handling are never cut for simplicity.
- Proportional effort: agent effort (reads, runs, review lenses, test tiers, delegated agents, tokens) is spent by the same Value test. Take the cheapest step that decides the question first (a targeted read or the narrowest check before a broad sweep or full suite), stop gathering once the evidence decides, never re-derive or re-verify what the run already established for inputs that have not changed since, and size test tiers and delegated agents to the change's risk, not its length (review lenses: `independent-review` Review policy). Decide what has a conventional default or is cheap to reverse and state the choice (Record assumptions below); the user decides only what an existing rule already reserves for them (such as global Critical Rules, Minimal-Code Discipline, Repo Toolchain Fit and SDLC merge confirmation, a stated compatibility obligation under Baseline, License stability, infrastructure approval under Scale, and the calling skill's own stops) and intent that is ambiguous with materially different outcomes. An unattended run applies its caller's needs-human signal instead of asking.
  - Done first: before building, name the narrowest runnable check that will show the change works (a regression test for a bug, an acceptance check for a feature), or why none can run; build until that check passes (with none, until) and the criteria the change touches are met, then stop building that change (discovered work follows its own rule).
  - Default path first: within what Value never cuts, the path a typical user takes is correct, tested and resilient before anything else. Other failure modes are taken in order of likelihood x impact / effort, and an unlikely input gets the framework's default refusal or error, not bespoke handling. Input crossing a trust boundary and cost that grows with stored data are never unlikely.
  - Record assumptions: a choice made without asking is stated in the PR body so review can catch a wrong one, apart from anything a held fix's rule keeps out of it. Assumptions take the pragmatic, scalable reading these criteria support (the right design for the change, sized to Scale), never by default the most minimal patch nor an over-engineered one; where intent is ambiguous with materially different outcomes and no existing rule decides it, ask the user as above.
  - Scripts over prose: a procedure agents run repeatedly that has a checkable result lives in a script, with a test or check in the repo's existing tooling, and agent instructions and skills name the script instead of restating its steps.
  - Always-loaded text stays small: instruction text loaded every session (such as a global rules block, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or a memory index) states rules and points to where procedures live; procedures live in skills or scripts loaded on demand, so every session does not pay for them.
- Findings are weighed the same way, each one. A confirmed defect is rare when it needs a coincidence such as a narrow race window or an unlikely ordering of events; input that crosses a trust boundary or that a caller can choose never makes it rare. It fails in the safe direction when it recovers by itself before any deadline it serves, and nothing is lost, exposed, duplicated or wrongly moved (money, access): it refuses or delays, an idempotent step repeats, derived or recreatable state is removed, or a view stays stale until the next read. Such a defect is rebutted with that likelihood and impact evidence, citing file:line of the safe outcome, or gets the smallest local fix where one exists. It never earns a new mechanism, table, lock scheme, redesign or refactor of the approach, whatever Design says. Actual data loss and security exposure still get fixed, however rare, and accessibility, and the resilience and scale work these criteria require, are never rebutted this way. Query cost that follows a growing table (Data access) is neither rare nor safe-direction: the growth is certain.
- Baseline by default: we are creating the baseline. Unless the user or repo states a compatibility obligation (a policy, a README stating a compatibility promise to consumers, or a configured package-validation baseline version; API baseline files that only guard against accidental breaks are not one):
  - Refactoring is approved where it makes code simpler, more maintainable or more scalable: it reduces complexity or risk, never relocates it. Churn without one of those gains is not approved. Consistency with the codebase beats local elegance unless the convention is the defect.
  - Breaking code and API changes are accepted; no backward compatibility, shims, deprecation paths, legacy accommodation or code kept only for past versions.
  - Code, comments, docs and instructions describe the current design only, never its history: no "previously", "renamed from", "old" or "legacy" notes. Git holds the history; records kept as history (changelogs and release notes, handoffs, review-yield tables, dated evidence) stay.
  - Data is the exception: applied migrations stay as written; changes to persisted or in-flight data (stored rows, queued and outbox messages, caches, serialized payloads, data exchanged between this system's own components during a mixed-version rollout) or deployed schema keep it readable through new, data-preserving migrations or a reader kept until it drains, with its removal condition, and irreversible data and schema operations still need confirmation.
- Design: solid, maintainable and scalable code is preferred over fast delivery or rounds of patching; the Value test above keeps it from over-engineering.
  - Build the right design for the change, even when it costs more than a narrow patch: the simplest design that is correct on every reachable case, DRY, maintainable and sized to the Scale criteria.
  - Refactor at the cause instead of patching: when a defect or review finding has its cause in the approach (one invariant, data path, ownership or state model), change the approach, not each symptom. This holds before review too: when a second fix for the same failure, invariant or flow fails, or a fix surfaces a new failure there, stop patching, name the shared cause and change the approach, taking only what `independent-review`'s redesign cycle could take here (its cannot-be-taken-here cases go to the user, or for an unattended run to its caller's needs-human signal) and recording any scope growth in the PR body; this does not count toward that cycle's redesign bounds, which own review-time redesign.
  - Reuse, then extend, then new: for any helper, engine, script or workflow the change needs, search the repo first (its existing skills and scripts, and the shared locations its facts file names: code map, shared package catalog); reuse what fits, else extend the existing one, else build new. Cross-cutting mechanisms follow Marks below. A new shared helper, script, engine or mechanism states the search that found none in the PR body and, for a delegated slice, in its REUSE report.
  - Foundation first: a type or mechanism provided by the shared packages the repo builds on (its facts file names their catalog) is used, never re-implemented. A gap there is another repository's work under the discovered-work rule (it goes to the user, or from a worker to its orchestrator), and a local stopgap carries its removal condition.
  - DRY: remove the duplication the change adds or touches by reusing the existing helper, or by extracting one reusable helper the call sites share (two or more real call sites count as callers; no speculative generality).
  - One decision point per rule: each business rule, policy, invariant, threshold or mapping is decided in one place that every caller uses, never re-decided or copied across layers, hosts or config. Example: an entity whose allowed actions depend on its status gets one state machine (states, allowed transitions and their guards in one table or type) that every handler, API, UI and job asks, instead of status checks spread across them.
  - One mechanism per job: each cross-cutting mechanism (locking, idempotency keys, the outbound-provider-call protocol, failure classification, the notification, alert and audit path, cache invalidation, access enforcement, the page state and refresh rule) has one implementation that every caller uses. A second one is a defect even when both work, except transiently between the slices of one recorded split consolidation, which completes before any feature slice uses it.
    - Marks: mark each mechanism a change needs reuse, extend or new, in that order of preference. Reuse where the repo has exactly one implementation for that job and it fits; extend where that one falls short or two or more exist (consolidate them into one, even when one already fits); new only where none exists or extending cannot meet the need.
    - Retirement: a consolidation or replacement records why, names every implementation it retires, moves every caller to the surviving one and deletes the retired ones, except a reader that persisted or in-flight data still needs, kept with its removal condition (global Data rule).
    - Access enforcement: authorization is one decision point, computed once per resource acted on (per request, or per item where a request or job acts on several) from its principal, action and resource, that every handler, background caller and UI asks. A lower layer enforcing the decision it is handed is not a second check, but recomputing it or applying divergent rules is. A job acting for a user (a message handler, sweep or bulk processor running as the stored caller) takes that user's decision, per item. A platform job, which runs with no requesting user, transitions the facts the decision reads (standing, lifecycle or policy, such as a billing sweep that suspends an account, or a data-exit sweep that moves a suspended one to terminated; its export or deletion of data is not a transition). Those transitions, and the reads their guards need, run through the lifecycle type that governs them and are not callers of the access decision; a request that triggers one takes its principal's decision first. The design record names each such transition with its lifecycle type and guard reads; the access decision stays the only reader of those facts for access. Any other read, write, export or delete of users' resources by a system job, in the same job or another, goes through the same decision point as a named service principal.
    - Page state and refresh rule: a UI defines once what a route or query change re-initializes and what it keeps, and a data component's refresh re-renders that component and what depends on its data, never remounting or resetting unrelated page state.
    - Example: every handler that charges a card takes its idempotency key from one key builder, instead of each formatting its own.
- Resilient and scalable by default: every change keeps working when a dependency falters and when load and data grow, without being asked. Calls subject to transient faults get the standard resilience mechanism with a timeout (Resilience); no instance holds state another request needs, and work that must survive a crash or exceeds a request's latency budget leaves the request (Scale); cost follows the work done, never the size of stored data (Data access). These are correctness at any load, not optimization. The files named hold the detail; tuning beyond them is sized by Load and measurement.
- Standards first: framework-native and well-known patterns before custom abstractions; a new dependency must clearly earn its place.
- License stability: prefer the platform and its first-party libraries, then open-source components under an open license, meaning an OSI-approved permissive (such as MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC or PostgreSQL) or weak-copyleft (such as MPL-2.0) one, governed by a foundation or a broad contributor base. This covers the project's build and runtime dependencies, self-hosted servers included; not developer tooling installed on machines or separately billed managed services.
  - New dependencies: one already under a source-available, commercial or otherwise more restrictive license, or one that already moved to such a license, is a dependency change the user approves first. One whose single vendor controls the copyright (or holds a CLA that lets it relicense) and sells a commercial edition is used only when no foundation- or community-governed alternative fits the need, with that reason recorded in the change.
  - Existing dependencies: one still on its last open version stays there and takes security fixes released under an open license; a fix released only under the new license goes to the user as a security finding. One already on a post-move version, or licensed by the user on purpose, is reported to the user once (not when the repo's dependency or license notes record it as deliberate; when the user confirms it is, add that note) and downgraded only with the user's approval. Replacing such a dependency, upgrading across the move or downgrading it is a dependency change the user approves first.
- Lean to operate: every log line, metric, retained file and background job justifies its cost.
- Load and measurement: performance work is sized to the load profile (users, request and message rates, data volume and expected growth; from the repo facts file or the user, else assumed and marked assumed) and is worth doing only where that load, or credible near-term growth in it, makes the gap cost something. "Measured" means existing evidence: telemetry (built-in framework and runtime instrumentation counts), a benchmark or load test in the repo, figures from the user, or a cost evident from code shape at a stated (not assumed) load profile, with the arithmetic recorded; without it a measurement-gated item waits, naming the measurement that would decide it. Correctness, security, required resilience and query cost that follows a growing table (Data access) are weighed at any load, never gated on a measurement; only an item its file marks measured waits for one.

## Packs

The rest of the criteria live in files beside this one, each titled with the name other skills cite (`engineering-criteria` Resilience means `resilience.md`; a citation of a bullet, such as Health and control or Retirement, names a bullet inside one of them or this file). This table is the one place that decides which a change needs. Files are delivered whole and by file, never retyped: copied into a reviewer's input folder, appended to a worker's prompt file with a shell copy, or named by path for an agent that can read this folder.

| A change that touches | Attach | The worker reports |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Any code, script or agent instruction | this file | REUSE: each new shared helper, script, engine or mechanism, with the searches run, the nearest existing one and the decision (reuse, extend, new) |
| Queries, EF model or configuration, indexes, migrations, raw SQL, bulk writes, transactions, reach or scope predicates | `data-access.md` | QUERIES (the inventory that file defines) |
| Outbound calls, retries, timeouts, and scripts, CI steps or tests that call the network | `resilience.md` | - |
| Background jobs, locks, shared state, caching, rate limits, probes, runtime configuration, messaging and events (the outbox, idempotent consumers), async IO and concurrency, work that must survive a crash or outlast a request | `scale.md` | - |
| Any logic change, test code, CI test triggers | `tests.md` | - |
| Logging, retention, deploy or backup scripts | `operations.md` | - |
| Public API, READMEs, agent instruction files | `documentation.md` | - |
| Entry points (endpoints, hubs, message or webhook handlers, jobs acting on users' data), authentication, authorization, tenancy, input from outside the process, secrets, personal data, files, outbound requests to caller-supplied addresses | `security.md` | ENTRY POINTS (the inventory that file defines) |
| Pages, components, client-side state | `ui.md` | - |

A file is added only for an escape that no file here owns, or for a class these criteria never cut that has no stated bar.

## Repo facts

A repository with product code records the facts these criteria cannot know in `docs/engineering-facts.md`, pointed to from its agent instructions: load profile; supported providers and other configuration axes, with the command per test tier; growing tables, with any bound on their row count; index convention; the query-check harness and how to add a case; shared building blocks (helper locations, code map, shared package catalog); gate tiers with their usual duration. Where it is absent, a reader derives what it needs from the code (a table is growing by Data access's own definition) and says "facts file absent; derived" in its report. An attended session may draft the file. An unattended run writes and files nothing for the gap, since the facts are the owner's to state: that line in its report is the record, and its caller's discovered-work rule does not apply. Values an agent derived stay marked assumed until the owner confirms them, so a derived load profile is assumed, never stated. Its absence never blocks.
